question: What material were the double-storeyed gates of Purana Qila primarily built with?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red sandstone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Purana Qila (पुराना किला) in Delhi was largely built during the reign of Sher Shah Suri and Humayun.

• Its massive double-storeyed gateways — Bara Darwaza, Humayun Darwaza and Talaqi Darwaza — were primarily constructed of red sandstone.

• Red sandstone was the favoured building stone of the Sur and Mughal builders because of its durability and rich colour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Purana Qila is regarded as one of the oldest forts of Delhi, associated with the ancient city of Indraprastha.

• The fort was later used by Humayun, who named his citadel Dinpanah.

some white marble was used for decorative inlay work only.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Marble was used only for decorative inlay and detailing, not for the main gates.

• opt (Option 3): Glazed tiles were used sparingly as ornamentation, not as the primary building material.

• opt (Option 4): Rubble was used as core filling in walls but was not the material of the ornamental gates.

question:
Fill in the blank:
The Tusu festival is primarily celebrated in the tribal belt of Jharkhand, especially around the area between ______, Tamar, and Raidih.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bundu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tusu (टुसू पर्व) is a popular harvest folk festival of the tribal belt of Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.

• It is celebrated mainly in the region around Bundu, Tamar and Raidih in Jharkhand.

• It is observed during the month of Poush (December–January) and is dedicated to an unmarried folk goddess, Tusu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The festival is marked by folk songs (Tusu geet) and the immersion of decorated bamboo-and-paper structures called 'chaudal'.

• It is a community festival largely led by young women of the region.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Dumka is a district in the Santhal Pargana region, not the core Tusu belt named here.

• opt (Option 3): Daltonganj (Medininagar) is in Palamu district in western Jharkhand.

• opt (Option 4): Chaibasa is the headquarters of West Singhbhum district, not the area referred to in the statement.

question: Who is credited with developing the modern notation system for Hindustani classical music and documenting compositions in the Kramik Pustak Maalika?
option_1: Ustad Allauddin Khan of Maihar Gharana
option_2: Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar of Gwalior
option_3: Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande of Bombay
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande of Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande (पंडित विष्णु नारायण भातखंडे) developed the modern notation system widely used in Hindustani classical music.

• He documented and standardised numerous compositions (bandishes) in his multi-volume work 'Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati' and the 'Kramik Pustak Maalika'.

• He is also famous for organising the ragas of Hindustani music into the ten-thaat classification system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bhatkhande (1860–1936) was born in Bombay and worked extensively to systematise and revive Hindustani classical music.

• He founded the Marris College of Music (now Bhatkhande Music Institute) in Lucknow.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Ustad Allauddin Khan of the Maihar Gharana was a legendary instrumentalist and guru, not the creator of this notation system.

• opt (Option 2): Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar popularised music education and founded the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya but used his own notation system.

• opt (Option 4): Saint Tyagaraja was a composer of the Carnatic (South Indian) tradition, not Hindustani music.

question:
Consider the following statements about service rules in table tennis:
1) At 10–10, service alternates every two points.
2) In the final doubles game, receiver order changes when one side reaches 5 points.
Which of the above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 2 is Correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In table tennis (टेबल टेनिस), service normally changes after every 2 points, but at 10–10 (deuce) service alternates after every single point — so statement 1 is wrong.

• In the final (deciding) game of a doubles match, the receiving pair changes its order of receiving as soon as one side reaches 5 points — so statement 2 is correct.

• Hence only statement 2 is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A game is won by the first player/pair to score 11 points, with a 2-point lead required.

• Ends are also changed when the first side reaches 5 points in the last possible game of a match.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Incorrect, as statement 1 is false; at 10–10 service alternates every point, not every two points.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect, because statement 1 is not correct.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect, since statement 2 is actually correct.

question: Under Pitt's India Act, what restriction was placed on the Governor General and Council?
option_1: They could not pass any civil law without Queen's consent.
option_2: They could not issue orders without majority support.
option_3: They were forbidden to declare war or make treaties without approval.
option_4: They had to resign after 5 years in office.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They were forbidden to declare war or make treaties without approval.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pitt's India Act of 1784 (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट) established a system of dual control over the East India Company by the Board of Control and the Court of Directors.

• It restricted the Governor General and Council from declaring war, entering into treaties or negotiating with Indian states without the prior approval of the authorities in England.

• The Act aimed to curb the aggressive expansionist and diplomatic freedom of the Company's officials.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Act was introduced by British PM William Pitt the Younger to rectify the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773.

• It gave the British Government direct control over the Company's civil, military and revenue affairs.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): There was no requirement of the Queen's consent for civil laws under this Act.

• opt (Option 2): The Governor General's Council did decide by majority, but this was not the special restriction introduced by Pitt's Act.

• opt (Option 4): There was no fixed rule compelling resignation after 5 years under Pitt's India Act.

question: What is meant by an "own goal" in football?
option_1: A goal scored by a goalkeeper
option_2: A goal scored from a penalty
option_3: A goal scored accidentally into one's own net
option_4: A goal scored during injury time
solution_text:
The correct answer is A goal scored accidentally into one's own net.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In football (फुटबॉल), an 'own goal' occurs when a player accidentally puts the ball into their own team's net.

• The goal is then counted in favour of the opposing team.

• It usually happens due to a mis-hit, deflection or defensive error while trying to clear the ball.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Own goals are officially credited to the last player of the defending team who touched the ball before it crossed the line.

• In records, own goals are often marked with the abbreviation 'OG'.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): A goal scored by a goalkeeper for their own side is a normal goal, not an own goal.

• opt (Option 2): A goal scored from a penalty is a penalty goal, credited to the scorer.

• opt (Option 4): A goal scored during injury time is simply a late goal, unrelated to the definition of an own goal.

question:
Consider the following statements about India's Winter Olympics participation:
1) Shiva Keshavan competed in six Games and introduced luge to India.
2) Arif Mohammad Khan was the first Indian to qualify for two alpine skiing events in 2022.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 both are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shiva Keshavan (शिवा केशवन) is India's most famous luge athlete who competed in six Winter Olympic Games and pioneered the sport of luge in India.

• Arif Mohammad Khan (Mohammad Arif Khan) became the first Indian to qualify for two alpine skiing events (Slalom and Giant Slalom) at the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics.

• Both the given statements are therefore correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shiva Keshavan set an Asian luge speed record during his career and represented India from 1998 to 2018.

• Beijing 2022 was Arif Khan's debut Winter Olympics, where he was India's sole representative.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Incorrect, because statement 2 is also true, not just statement 1.

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect, because statement 1 is also true.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are factually correct.

question: Which 2024 India–Bangladesh energy project involves a 765 kV cross-border transmission line to boost hydroelectric trade across multiple countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Katihar–Parbotipur–Bornagar Interconnection Project.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Katihar–Parbatipur–Baranagar (कटिहार–परबतीपुर–बोरनगर) project is a 765 kV cross-border high-capacity transmission line linking India and Bangladesh.

• It is designed to strengthen regional power connectivity and facilitate hydroelectric power trade across countries such as India, Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan.

• The project was reviewed and pushed forward as part of India–Bangladesh energy cooperation in 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It runs from Katihar in Bihar (India) through Parbatipur to Baranagar in Bangladesh.

• Such interconnections support India's vision of a regional power grid and sub-regional electricity markets under BBIN cooperation.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The 'Agartala–Parbotipur–Guwahati Transmission Grid' is not the recognised 765 kV project.

• opt (Option 3): The 'Jalpaiguri–Chattogram Power Corridor' is not a real named project in this context.

• opt (Option 4): The 'Siliguri–Bogura–Mymensingh HVDC Link' does not correspond to this 765 kV initiative.

question:
Consider the following statements about the book 'Being Indian' by Pavan K. Varma:
1) The book won the Vodafone Crossword Book Award for exploring Indian identity and culture.
2) It received the Sahitya Akademi Award for its contributions to Indian English poetry.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statement 1 is correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Being Indian' (बीइंग इंडियन) by Pavan K. Varma is a non-fiction work analysing Indian identity, character and culture.

• The book was recognised through the Vodafone Crossword Book Award, making statement 1 correct.

• It is a work of non-fiction prose, so it could not receive a Sahitya Akademi Award for Indian English poetry — statement 2 is false.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pavan K. Varma is a former diplomat, author and politician known for several works on Indian society.

• 'Being Indian' explores paradoxes in Indian attitudes towards power, wealth, democracy and spirituality.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect, because the book is prose, not poetry, and did not win a Sahitya Akademi Award for poetry.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect, since statement 2 is false.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect, because statement 1 is indeed true.

question:
Fill in the blank:
Javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra won India's first-ever gold at the World Athletics Championships in ______ in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Budapest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Neeraj Chopra (नीरज चोपड़ा) won India's first-ever gold medal at the World Athletics Championships in the men's javelin throw.

• This historic gold was won at Budapest, Hungary, in 2023 with a throw of 88.17 m.

• He had earlier won a silver at the 2022 World Championships in Eugene, USA.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Neeraj Chopra is also the Olympic gold medallist from the Tokyo 2020 Games in javelin throw.

• With this win he became the first Indian to hold the World Championship title in athletics.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): At Eugene (2022) he won silver, not gold.

• opt (Option 2): Tokyo hosted the 2020 Olympics where he won gold, but that is not the World Athletics Championships.

• opt (Option 4): Doha hosted the 2019 World Championships, where India did not win this javelin gold.

question: Who launched the campaign "Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam " in 2024, encouraging citizens to plant trees in honor of their mothers and Mother Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' (एक पेड़ माँ के नाम) campaign was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2024.

• It encourages citizens to plant a tree in honour of their mother and Mother Earth.

• It was launched around World Environment Day (5 June) 2024 as a mass movement for environmental protection.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The campaign is aligned with the 'Mission LiFE' (Lifestyle for Environment) initiative.

• It aims to promote large-scale afforestation and emotional connect with nature.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Leena Nandan served as a senior official (Secretary) in the Environment Ministry but did not launch this campaign.

• opt (Option 3): Bhupender Yadav is the Union Environment Minister who supported the drive but is not credited as its launcher.

• opt (Option 4): Ashwini Vaishnaw is a Union Minister for other portfolios and is unrelated to launching this campaign.

question: What causes a river to develop meanders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lateral erosion in flat terrain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A meander (विसर्प) is a bend or loop that develops in the course of a river, mainly in its middle and lower stages.

• It is caused by lateral (sideways) erosion of the river banks in gently sloping or flat terrain.

• The river erodes the outer (concave) bank and deposits material on the inner (convex) bank, gradually forming wide loops.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Extreme meanders can get cut off from the main channel to form an ox-bow lake.

• Meandering is characteristic of a mature river flowing over a plain with low gradient.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): High-altitude origin relates to a river's youthful, fast-flowing vertical-erosion stage, not meandering.

• opt (Option 2): Sudden tectonic uplift generally leads to rejuvenation and gorge formation, not meanders.

• opt (Option 4): Ocean currents act in the sea and do not cause a river to meander.

question:
Fill in the Blanks:
NISAR maps the global surface every _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12 days.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NISAR (निसार, NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint Earth-observation satellite mission of NASA and ISRO.

• It scans and maps almost the entire global land and ice surface once every 12 days.

• This repeat cycle allows precise monitoring of changes in the Earth's surface.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• NISAR uses dual-frequency radar — NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band.

• It helps study ecosystems, ice-sheet dynamics, natural hazards, land deformation and sea-level rise.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): '3 days' does not match the mission's designed repeat cycle.

• opt (Option 3): '24 hrs' is far too short for its global mapping cycle.

• opt (Option 4): '5 days' is not the correct repeat interval for NISAR.

question: Which of the below statements on the plant hormones is INCORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethylene promotes seed germination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ethylene (एथिलीन) is a gaseous plant hormone mainly associated with the ripening of fruits, senescence and abscission of leaves and flowers.

• Its primary role is not the promotion of seed germination, so this statement is incorrect.

• Since the question asks for the INCORRECT statement, ethylene promoting seed germination is the answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ethylene also promotes the ripening of fruits and is used commercially in fruit-ripening chambers.

• It can break dormancy and stimulate flowering in some plants like pineapple.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Correct statement — auxins promote cell elongation and overall growth.

• opt (Option 2): Correct statement — cytokinins delay ageing (senescence) of plant tissues.

• opt (Option 4): Correct statement — gibberellins promote stem elongation and internode growth.

question: Which of the following disputes falls under the Supreme Court's exclusive original jurisdiction as per Article 131 of the Indian Constitution?
option_2: Election disputes of MPs and MLAs
option_3: Disputes between Centre and one or more States
solution_text:
The correct answer is Disputes between Centre and one or more States.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 131 (अनुच्छेद 131) of the Indian Constitution gives the Supreme Court exclusive original jurisdiction in disputes of a federal nature.

• This covers disputes between the Centre and one or more States, between the Centre and States on one side and other States on the other, and between two or more States.

• 'Exclusive' means no other court can hear such disputes, and 'original' means they can be brought directly to the Supreme Court.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The dispute must involve a question of legal right, not merely a political one.

• Article 131 does not extend to disputes arising out of certain pre-Constitution treaties or agreements.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Inter-State water disputes are dealt with under Article 262 and are generally kept out of ordinary court jurisdiction by law.

• opt (Option 2): Election disputes of MPs and MLAs are decided by High Courts through election petitions, not under Article 131.

• opt (Option 4): Appeals against High Court decisions come under the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction, not its original jurisdiction.

question: If the resistance of a conductor is doubled while keeping the potential difference across its ends constant, what will happen to the current flowing through it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is It will halve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Ohm's law (ओम का नियम), current I = V / R, where V is the potential difference and R is the resistance.

• At constant V, current is inversely proportional to resistance.

• If R is doubled, the current becomes half of its original value.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ohm's law holds for ohmic conductors at constant temperature.

• The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω) and of current is the ampere (A).

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Current would double only if resistance were halved, not doubled.

• opt (Option 3): Current cannot remain unchanged when resistance changes and voltage is fixed.

• opt (Option 4): Current would not quadruple; that is not consistent with Ohm's law here.

question: Under Bharatiya Nagarik suraksha Samhita(BNSS), the period for default bail in minor offences is capped at?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60 days.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता) replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).

• The right to default (statutory) bail arises when the investigation is not completed within the prescribed period.

• For offences punishable with imprisonment up to ten years (minor category), the period is capped at 60 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• For offences punishable with death, life imprisonment or imprisonment of ten years or more, the period is 90 days.

• Default bail is a statutory right of the accused and is granted when the charge sheet is not filed within the time limit.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): '30 days' is not the prescribed period for default bail in minor offences.

• opt (Option 2): '45 days' is not a period fixed for default bail under BNSS.

• opt (Option 4): '90 days' applies to more serious offences, not minor ones.

question: Which scheme promotes crop diversification through cluster-based planning?
option_1: PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan)
solution_text:
The correct answer is RKVY (Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (राष्ट्रीय कृषि विकास योजना) promotes overall agricultural growth including crop diversification through cluster-based and area-specific planning.

• It gives States flexibility to plan and implement agriculture and allied-sector projects according to local needs.

• Crop Diversification Programme is implemented as a component under this scheme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• RKVY was launched in 2007 and later reoriented as RKVY-RAFTAAR (Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied sector Rejuvenation).

• It encourages farmers to shift from water-intensive crops such as paddy to pulses, oilseeds and other alternatives.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): PM-AASHA is focused on ensuring remunerative prices (MSP support) to farmers, not cluster-based crop diversification.

• opt (Option 3): SMAM aims at promoting farm mechanization, not crop diversification.

• opt (Option 4): AIF provides financing for post-harvest and agriculture infrastructure, not diversification planning.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:
Assertion (A): PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 in AQI.
Reason (R): PM2.5 particles are smaller and can reach deep into the lungs and bloodstream.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
option_3: A is true, but R is false.
option_4: A is false, but R is true.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PM2.5 (सूक्ष्म कण) refers to particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less, while PM10 is up to 10 micrometres.

• PM2.5 is more harmful because its very small size lets it penetrate deep into the lungs and even enter the bloodstream.

• Thus, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Both PM2.5 and PM10 are key pollutants monitored in the Air Quality Index (AQI).

• Long-term exposure to PM2.5 is linked to respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect, because R does correctly explain A.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect, because R is true, not false.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect, because A is true, not false.

question: Which national park reported a successful tiger population rise in 2024, reaching over 150 tigers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Corbett.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jim Corbett National Park (कॉर्बेट राष्ट्रीय उद्यान) in Uttarakhand reported a strong tiger population, crossing over 150 tigers.

• Corbett has consistently recorded the highest tiger density and one of the largest tiger populations among India's tiger reserves.

• It is a leading example of successful tiger conservation under Project Tiger.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Corbett, established in 1936, is India's oldest national park and the first to come under Project Tiger (1973).

• It lies in the Nainital and Pauri Garhwal districts of Uttarakhand.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Ranthambore in Rajasthan has a notable tiger population but not the figure referred to here.

• opt (Option 2): Nagarhole National Park in Karnataka is a major tiger habitat but is not the park mentioned in the statement.

• opt (Option 4): Satpura in Madhya Pradesh is a tiger reserve but does not match this specific figure.

question:
Fill in the Blank:
Doctrine of Severability allows the ______ part of a law to be retained.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Valid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Doctrine of Severability (पृथक्करणीयता का सिद्धांत) states that if only a part of a law is unconstitutional, only that offending part is struck down.

• The valid part of the law, which can operate independently, is retained and remains enforceable.

• It is derived from Article 13 of the Constitution, which declares laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void only to the extent of the inconsistency.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The doctrine is also called the Doctrine of Separability.

• It was applied in cases such as A. K. Gopalan v. State of Madras.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): A repealed part of a law no longer exists, so it cannot be 'retained'.

• opt (Option 2): The inconsistent part is the portion that is struck down, not retained.

• opt (Option 4): The unconstitutional part is exactly what is removed under this doctrine.

question:
Read the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): Aluminium smelting is the most important metallurgical industry in India.
Reason (R): Aluminium is used in the manufacture of aircraft, wires, and utensils.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is false, but R is true.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aluminium smelting (एल्युमीनियम प्रगलन) is the second most important metallurgical industry in India, after iron and steel — so the Assertion is false.

• Aluminium is indeed used in making aircraft, electrical wires and household utensils, so the Reason is true.

• Hence the Assertion is false while the Reason is a correct statement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Aluminium is valued for being light, strong, a good conductor of electricity and highly malleable.

• It is obtained from the ore bauxite through electrolytic reduction of alumina.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Incorrect, because the Assertion itself is false.

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect, since the Assertion is not true.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect, because the Reason is a true statement, not false.

question:
Match the dance with its prime social/religious context:
Dance | social/religious context
1. Rauf | A. Eid & spring-wedding festivities
2. Karma | B. Bhadra Ekadashi agrarian ritual
3. Tamasha | C. Night-long folk-theatre in Shimga season
4. Jhumar | D. Post-monsoon tea-garden recreations
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-A 2-B 3-C 4-D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rauf (रौफ) is a folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir performed by women during Eid and spring/wedding festivities — 1-A.

• Karma is a tribal dance associated with the Bhadra Ekadashi (Karma) agrarian ritual celebrated in central and eastern India — 2-B.

• Tamasha is a Maharashtrian folk-theatre form known for its night-long performances, linked to the Shimga (Holi) season — 3-C.

• Jhumar is associated with post-monsoon recreations, including those in tea-garden communities — 4-D.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rauf is characterised by rhythmic footwork and rows of women facing each other.

• Tamasha traditionally includes music, dance and dramatic performances popular in rural Maharashtra.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect, as it wrongly swaps Karma and Tamasha with contexts B and C.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect, as it wrongly matches Rauf with B and Karma with A.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect, as it wrongly swaps the contexts of Jhumar and Tamasha (D and C).

question: Which pair correctly matches atmosphere layer & feature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Troposphere - weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The troposphere (क्षोभमंडल) is the lowest layer of the atmosphere where almost all weather phenomena such as clouds, rain and storms occur.

• It contains most of the atmosphere's water vapour and dust, which drive weather activity.

• Hence the correct match is Troposphere – weather.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ozone layer that absorbs ultraviolet radiation is present in the stratosphere, not the thermosphere.

• Meteors mostly burn up in the mesosphere, while many satellites orbit in the thermosphere/exosphere region.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Incorrect, because ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, not the thermosphere.

• opt (Option 3): Incorrect, because satellites generally orbit in the thermosphere and above, not the mesosphere.

• opt (Option 4): Incorrect, because meteors burn up mainly in the mesosphere, not the stratosphere.

question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Concurrent List allows both Centre and States to legislate.
2. In case of conflict, State law prevails over Union law.
Which of the above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Concurrent List (समवर्ती सूची) in the Seventh Schedule allows both the Centre and the States to make laws on the subjects listed in it — statement 1 is correct.

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent subject, the Union (Central) law generally prevails, not the State law — statement 2 is incorrect.

• Hence only statement 1 is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This principle of Union supremacy on the Concurrent List is contained in Article 254 of the Constitution.

• A State law can prevail only if it has received the President's assent, and even then Parliament can override it.

NOTE
